purpose: Interactive HTML maps — watershed boundaries, gauge locations, stream networks

folium.Map.note: tiles='CartoDB positron' gives a clean, publication-neutral basemap. Default is OpenStreetMap.
folium.Map.example: m = folium.Map(location=[lat, lon], zoom_start=9, tiles='CartoDB positron')

folium.GeoJson.note: Pass the GeoJSON as a dict or file path. Geometries must be in EPSG:4326.

gotchas: CRS requirement: folium always expects EPSG:4326 (lon, lat) — reproject GeoDataFrames with gdf.to_crs('EPSG:4326') before passing.
GeoJSON coordinate order: GeoJSON uses [longitude, latitude] — the opposite of many Python libraries that use (lat, lon).
Saving: m.save('map.html') writes a standalone HTML file (~1 MB). m._repr_html_() works in Jupyter but not as a file.
Marker popups: folium.Popup(html_str, max_width=300) — always set max_width to prevent truncation.
Layer control: folium.LayerControl().add_to(m) must be added AFTER all layers to show all layers in the control.
Large GeoJSON: passing a GeoDataFrame with thousands of rows will produce a very large HTML file. Simplify geometry first: gdf.geometry.simplify(tolerance=0.001).
Choropleth: requires a pandas Series for the data argument and a GeoJSON with matching keys. Use key_on='feature.properties.id' to match.
Tiles alternatives: 'OpenStreetMap', 'CartoDB positron', 'CartoDB dark_matter', 'Stamen Terrain' (may require API key in newer versions).

common_patterns.watershed_map:
import folium
m = folium.Map(location=[lat, lon], zoom_start=9, tiles='CartoDB positron')
folium.GeoJson(watershed_geojson, name='Watershed', style_function=lambda x: {'color': 'steelblue', 'fillOpacity': 0.1}).add_to(m)
folium.CircleMarker(location=[lat, lon], radius=8, color='red', fill=True, popup=f'Gauge {gauge_id}').add_to(m)
folium.LayerControl().add_to(m)
m.save('watershed_map.html')
